turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that his actions had consequences, and that if he continued to oppress Nikhil's tenantry, he would not hesitate to take measures to protect them.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Sandip if there was nothing he could do to prevent such conflicts, as they seemed to be causing a great deal of unease among the villagers.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Bimala that she should not be so concerned about the petty squabbles between zamindars, for she was a poetess, not a politician, and that she should focus on her art, not on the petty intrigues of the estate owners.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil turned to Sandip with a stern expression and told him that his flippant attitude was a luxury he could no longer afford, as the situation was becoming increasingly volatile.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala turned to Nikhil and asked if the consequences he spoke of were something that could be easily resolved through words alone.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that he was as concerned about the tenantry as he was about the state of his own poetry, which was rapidly losing its beauty due to Nikhil's constant meddling.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that his words were a reflection of his lack of understanding of the gravity of the situation, and that he was willing to take drastic measures to ensure the safety of the tenantry.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala turned to Nikhil with a thoughtful expression, asking what kind of measures he had in mind to ensure the safety of the tenantry.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip told Nikhil that he was so filled with fear of the Mussulmans that he was beginning to think he needed to write a poem about their bravery, just to calm his nerves.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil insisted that Sandip should not underestimate the growing tensions between the tenantry and the Mussulmans, and that he needed to take concrete actions to protect the land and the people.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Nikhil if he had considered the potential consequences of taking drastic measures on the tenantry, and how it might affect their livelihoods and relationships with the land.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip laughed and said that Nikhil was being overly dramatic, that the Mussulmans were just trying to assert their power, and that it was laughable to think they were a threat to him or his land.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil told Sandip that his flippant attitude would only embolden the Mussulmans, and that he needed to be taken seriously if he wanted to protect his land and his people.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Nikhil to explain his proposal for protecting the land and the tenantry, and how he envisioned the implementation of his plan.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip snickered and told Nikhil that his warnings were as thrilling as a bad Bengali romance novel, and that he had a better chance of winning a prize for his poetry than he did of being attacked by the Mussulmans.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil warned Sandip that his mockery would not be tolerated, and that he would not hesitate to take action if his safety or the safety of his people was threatened.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Sandip if he truly believed that his words and actions would not have consequences for the people who lived on their land.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Sandip turned to Nikhil and told him that he was still waiting for the local Mussulmans to stage a coup, but so far, all they had done was steal his prize-winning mangoes.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Nikhil demanded that Sandip put aside his frivolous remarks and listen to the serious concerns that had been voiced by the local Mussulmans.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Bimala asked Nikhil if he had considered the possibility that the Mussulmans' grievances were not just about land or power, but also about the treatment they had received at the hands of the zamindars.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Bimala where she would go, addressing her as the Queen.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he kept Browning among his books, reminding him of a contest they had over translating lines from Browning, and inquiring if Nikhil remembered it.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil and Bimala that he had managed to translate the lines into Bengali, but the result was unlikely to be well-received, and that he had once thought he was on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence had intervened to prevent it, and he recalled old Dakshina's poetry.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Bimala that it was pointless to search the bookshelves, as Nikhil no longer read poetry since his marriage, but that he, Sandip, was about to be afflicted with the 'fever fit of poesy' again.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil warned Sandip that he had come to give him a warning.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was warning him about the 'fever fit of poesy'.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that for some time, Mahomedan preachers had been stirring up the local Mussulmans, who were angry with Sandip and might attack him at any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he had come to advise him to flee.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had come to give him information, not advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip told Nikhil that if the estates were his, a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for him, and that Nikhil should intimidate the preachers instead of frightening him, and that Nikhil's weakness was also affecting his neighbouring zamindars.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that he had not offered him advice, and that he wished Sandip would refrain from giving him his advice, as it was useless, and that there was another thing he wanted to tell Sandip, namely that Sandip and his followers had been secretly oppressing Nikhil's tenantry, and that he could no longer allow that, so he must ask Sandip to leave his territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he was threatening him with fear of the Mussulmans, or if there was another fear he had to threaten him with.
